Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Toghon Temür is an astronomer. Toghon Temür acceded to the throne in 1333 after years of succession disputes following his father's death.
Who among these is a mathematician?
John Horton Conway is a mathematician. John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 – 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
What is the atomic number of Caesium?
Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
What is the atomic number of Tungsten?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
In what year did Hamish Harding die?
Hamish Harding: George Hamish Livingston Harding (24 June 1964 – 18 June 2023) was a British businessman, pilot and adventurer based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
In what year was Pluto discovered?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
TypeScript: Anders Hejlsberg. TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
Pethidine: Pfizer. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.
In which country is Kazan phenomenon?
Kazan phenomenon: Soviet Union. The Kazan mafia was known to be particularly cruel in their extortion tactics, and periodically brought in reinforcements from Tatarstan.
Who is credited with discovering Seaborgium?
Seaborgium: Yuri Oganessian. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen cyanide?
Hydrogen cyanide: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula H−C≡N.
Who is credited with discovering Tungsten?
Tungsten: Juan José Elhuyar. Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
Home to both edible and poisonous species, this fungal genus supplies the West's most popular cultivated mushrooms, including the everyday button mushroom — which genus is it?
Agaricus is a genus of mushroom-forming fungi containing both edible and poisonous species, with over 400 members worldwide and possibly again as many disputed or newly discovered species.

This central nervous system stimulant treats ADHD and narcolepsy today, but was once prescribed for nasal congestion and depression, and remains tightly controlled due to its abuse potential — name the drug?

Amphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy; it is also used to treat binge eating disorder in the form of lisdexamfetamine.
More than 500 orb-weaving spider species, including the familiar garden spider, belong to this genus first classified in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus is a genus of common orb-weaving spiders with more than 500 species, among which are the European garden spider and the barn spider.
One of the first grains ever domesticated, this cereal crop was cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9000 BC and later spread throughout Eurasia by 2000 BC — name the grain?
Barley (Hordeum vulgare), a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.
So dense that not even light can escape its gravity, this astronomical object's boundary of no return is called the event horizon — name it?
Black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.
Splitting from the windpipe at the carina into a right and left branch, this airway keeps forking into ever-smaller tubes until it's too narrow for cartilage support — what is it?
Bronchus (pl.: bronchi) is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.
From starch that stores energy to the cellulose that stiffens plants and the chitin in insect shells, this biomolecule family is essentially sugars and their derivatives — what is it?
Carbohydrate is a sugar (saccharide) or a sugar derivative.

The smallest recognized dog breed in the world, this Mexican toy breed has large erect ears and a rounded skull, and its genes carry a trace of pre-Columbian indigenous American dog ancestry — which breed?

Chihuahua (dog breed) is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world. It is primarily kept as a companion animal and is characterized by its compact size, large erect ears, and rounded skull.
Native to Africa, Arabia and India, this semi-succulent herb smells like oregano and is known by names like Spanish thyme and Mexican mint — which plant?
Coleus amboinicus is a species of semi-succulent perennial plant in the family Lamiaceae.
These echinoderms come in stalked "sea lily" and free-swimming "feather star" forms, with mouths on their upper surface ringed by feeding arms — what class of marine animal is it?
Crinoid are marine invertebrates that make up the class Crinoidea.
This biological process breaks down large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components for absorption into the bloodstream, via both mechanical and chemical means. What is it?
Digestion is the breakdown of large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components so that they can be absorbed into the blood plasma.

This order of about 1,000 predatory fish species undergoes dramatic transformation from a distinctive larval stage to its adult form, and includes roughly 20 different families — what are these long, snake-like fish called?
Eel are ray-finned fish belonging to the order Anguilliformes, which consists of eight suborders, 20 families, 164 genera, and about 1000 species.
Also called grain alcohol, this volatile compound with the formula C2H5OH is the active ingredient in every alcoholic beverage — what is it?
Ethanol (also called ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol, drinking alcohol, or simply alcohol) is an organic compound with the chemical formula CH3CH2OH.
This everyday bodily process — expelling gas from the intestines through the anus — has its own dedicated field of scientific study named after it: what's the term for the process itself?
Flatulence is the expulsion of gas from the intestines via the anus, commonly referred to as farting.
This field of study examines how a country's physical geography shapes its politics and its relations with other nations — what field is it?
Geopolitics (from Ancient Greek g 'earth, land' and politik 'politics') is the study of the effects of Earth's geography on politics and international relations.
Endemic to Africa and among the oldest of the gallinaceous birds, this family branched off before New World quail evolutionarily — name the birds?
Guinea fowl are birds of the family Numididae in the order Galliformes.
Planted for land reclamation thanks to its nitrogen-fixing, erosion-resisting root system, this deciduous shrub genus's berries also show up in human and animal food products — what genus is it?
Hippophae is a genus of flowering plants in the family Elaeagnaceae.

Once diagnosed almost exclusively in women as a physical illness in the 19th century, this term for ungovernable emotional excess later became the focus of research by Freud and Charcot — what is this condition called?
Hysteria is a term used to mean ungovernable emotional excess and can refer to a temporary state of mind or emotion.
This Canadian-American physical educator invented an entire sport, wrote its original rule book after moving to the United States, and founded the University of Kansas's program in 1898 — who is he?
James Naismith (November 6, 1861 - November 28, 1939) was a Canadian-American physical educator, physician, Christian chaplain, and sports coach, best known as the inventor of the game of basketball.
One species of this succulent plant genus, native mainly to Madagascar, became one of the first plants ever sent into space aboard a Soviet space station in 1979 — what genus is it?
Kalanchoe (also called "kalanche" or "kalancho"), is a genus of about 125 species of tropical, succulent plants in the stonecrop family Crassulaceae, mainly native to Madagascar and tropical Africa.
Caused by a specific type of waterborne bacteria, this form of atypical pneumonia brings cough, fever, muscle pain, and headache within days of exposure — what's it called?
Legionnaires' disease is a form of atypical pneumonia caused by any species of Legionella bacteria, quite often Legionella pneumophila.

Fatigue, memory problems, breathlessness, and sleep trouble that the WHO marks as setting in three months after infection — symptoms that vanish and reappear for weeks or years. What condition is this?
Long COVID is a group of health problems persisting or developing after an initial period of COVID19 from 2 infection.
An autosomal dominant flaw in the fibrillin-making FBN1 gene gives this disorder its tell-tale look — tall, long-limbed, double-jointed — while quietly threatening the aorta — what is it?
Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multi-systemic genetic disorder that affects the connective tissue.
This field's founding body, the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures, grew out of an 1875 convention and eventually gave the world the International System of Units — what is this study called?
Metrology is the scientific study of measurement.
This small green legume, cultivated widely across East and South Asia, is used in both savory dishes and sweet desserts — what is it?
Mung bean (Vigna radiata) is a plant species in the legume family.
Born in the Austro-Hungarian Empire and emigrating to the US in 1884, he's known for pioneering the AC electricity system. Who?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 - 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
Listed by Ptolemy and named for a hunter in Greek myth, this winter constellation boasts the supergiant stars Rigel and Betelgeuse and a famous short, straight line of three stars — which is it?
Orion (constellation) is a prominent set of stars visible during winter in the northern celestial hemisphere.
About 3,000 varieties of this apple-like fruit exist worldwide, and its fermented juice is known as perry — which fruit is it?
Pear are a genus of trees, Pyrus, in the family Rosaceae, that bear an edible apple-like fruit of the same name.

This subdiscipline of biology examines how organisms, organs, cells, and biomolecules carry out their chemical and physical functions, and its name derives from Greek words for 'nature' and 'study of' — what is it?
Physiology (from Ancient Greek (phsis) 'nature, origin' and - (-loga) 'study of') is the scientific study of functions and mechanisms in a living system.
Which compound pulls double duty as a dietary iodine supplement and as the pill that protects the thyroid gland during radiation emergencies?
Potassium iodide (KI) is a chemical compound, medication, and dietary supplement.
Powered by a supermassive black hole accreting gas at its center, this extremely luminous type of galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy thousands of times over. What is it?
Quasar is an extremely luminous active galactic nucleus (AGN).
He'd spent years building and selling theremins toward a Cornell physics PhD before unveiling, in 1964, the first commercial instrument of its kind — which American electronics pioneer was this?
Robert Moog (MOHG; May 23, 1934 - August 21, 2005) was an American electronics engineer and electronic music pioneer.
Spanning continents from North America to temperate Asia, this genus covers the majority of the world's common bushy-tailed squirrels — which genus?
Sciurus (or) contains most of the common, bushy-tailed squirrels in North America, Europe, temperate Asia, Central America and South America.
The brightest star in the night sky, this star sits in the constellation Canis Major and is actually a binary system paired with a faint white dwarf companion — name the star?
Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, located in the southern constellation of Canis Major.
This round, gram-positive germ lives harmlessly on most people's skin and noses, but turn opportunistic and it triggers abscesses, sinus infections, and food poisoning. What is it?

Staphylococcus aureus is a gram-positive spherically shaped bacterium, a member of the Bacillota, and is a usual member of the microbiota of the body, frequently found in the upper respiratory tract and on the skin.

Named after a figure from Greek mythology condemned to eternal frustration, this hard, corrosion-resistant blue-gray metal, atomic number 73, is mined alongside the chemically similar niobium in the ore known as coltan. What element is this?
Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.

Proposing an information management system in March 1989 and implementing the first successful client-server exchange that November, this English computer scientist invented HTML, HTTP and the URL system — who is he?
Tim Berners-Lee (born 8 June 1955), also known as TimBL, is an English computer scientist best known as the inventor of the World Wide Web, HTML, the URL system, and HTTP.
What is the medical term for having dangerously high levels of urea in the blood, typically caused by kidney failure?

Uremia is the condition of having high levels of urea in the blood. It is the signs, symptoms and results from laboratory tests which result from inadequate excretory, regulatory, and endocrine function of the kidneys.
He co-developed the V-2 at Peenemünde — the first artificial object to cross the Kármán line into space — before bringing his rocketry to the United States; who was this engineer?
Wernher von Braun (23 March 1912 - 16 June 1977) was a German American aerospace engineer and space architect.

Unlike a user interface, which links a computer to a person, this software connection lets programs talk directly to each other — and the standard describing it is called its specification. What's the three-letter term?
API: Connection between computers or programs.
Nicknamed the 'killer' variety for its aggressive defense of the hive, this hybrid pollinating insect escaped Brazilian quarantine in 1957 and reached Texas by 1990 — which insect is it?
Africanized bee: Hybrid species of bee. The African honey bee was first introduced to Brazil in 1956 to increase honey production, but 26 swarms escaped quarantine in 1957.
Unlike its bulb-forming relative, the common onion, this perennial vegetable never forms a bulb and owes one of its names to its hollow, tube-like leaves — which plant?
Allium fistulosum: Species of plant. The species is very similar in taste and odor to the related common onion, Allium cepa, and hybrids between the two (tree onions) exist.
This Russian physicist miraculously survived a 1978 accident in which a high-energy proton beam from a particle accelerator passed directly through his skull — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski: Soviet and Russian scientist (born 1942)
Known by common names like greenfly and blackfly, these small sap-sucking insects reproduce via live-born nymphs without males, a trick called telescoping generations — what are they?
Aphid: Superfamily of insects. The group includes the fluffy white woolly aphids.
This common eye condition occurs when the cornea or lens is slightly egg-shaped rather than spherical, causing blurred vision at every distance?
This Caltech experimental physicist shared the 2017 Nobel with Rainer Weiss and Kip Thorne for the LIGO detector and the observation of gravitational waves — who is he?
Barry Barish: American physicist and Nobel Laureate (born 1936)

Having evolved independently at least 94 separate times — first in octocorals some 540 million years ago — this living glow lights up fireflies, deep-sea fish, fungi and dinoflagellates alike; what is it?
Bioluminescence: Emission of light by a living organism.

Despite lacking the tight head of typical cabbage, this leafy Chinese vegetable has a flavor often compared to spinach and water chestnuts, with a milder white bulb and stronger-tasting green leaves — what vegetable is it?
Bok choy: Subspecies of flowering plant.
With a large head, deep facial folds, and a flat face with a jutting lower jaw, this British breed's ancestors were once used for baiting cattle before the sport was banned in 1835 — which breed?
Bulldog: British breed of dog. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.
This Sicilian pastry is a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with sweet ricotta, dressed up with candied orange zest in Palermo or chopped pistachios in Catania — what treat is it?
Cannoli: Italian ricotta-filled pastry. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
Found across North America (and one Siberian species in Asia), these small striped squirrels stash food in their cheek pouches to store for winter — what are they?
Native to Indonesia's Maluku Islands, these aromatic flower buds flavor your food but also turn up in toothpaste and soaps — what spice are they?
Clove: Spice made from flower buds.
Spanning information theory and cryptography at one end and hardware design at the other, this field is broadly described as the study of computation, information, and automation — what is it?
Computer science: Study of computation. Algorithms and data structures are central to computer science.
Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the trachea and announces itself with an unmistakable barking, brassy cough — what's it called?
Croup: Respiratory infection often caused by a virus.

Nicknamed the 'Wooden Wonder' for its mostly-timber airframe, this WWII British warplane was among the fastest operational aircraft of 1941 and later moonlighted as a high-speed courier for a national airline — what was it?
De Havilland Mosquito: British multi-role combat aircraft of WW2.
This category of mental health conditions involves an unconscious defense mechanism that fragments consciousness, memory, and identity to protect against traumatic stress — what is it called?
Dissociative disorder: Set of mental health conditions.
A pregnancy complication where the embryo attaches outside the uterus, classically presenting with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. What is this condition?
Ectopic pregnancy: Female reproductive system health issue.
Since the 1960s, growing movements have pushed governments to restrain activities that damage the natural world and its resources — what is this broad field of effort called?
Environmental protection: Practice of protecting the natural environment.
Sporting pinkish-brown plumage, a black tail and a flash of bright blue on the wing, this woodland member of the crow family ranges from western Europe to the Indian subcontinent — which bird?
Eurasian jay: Species of bird. It has pinkish brown plumage with a black stripe on each side of a whitish throat, a bright blue panel on the upper wing and a black tail.
This anaerobic metabolic process, used by humans to preserve and flavor food for some 13,000 years, breaks down sugars to generate ATP when oxygen is scarce — what's it called?
Fermentation: Metabolic redox process producing energy in the absence of oxygen.
Called the "father of modern parasitology," this Italian physician-poet famously dismantled spontaneous generation by showing that maggots hatch from fly eggs — who was he?
Francesco Redi: Italian naturalist and poet. Francesco Redi (18 February 1626 – 1 March 1697) was an Italian physician, naturalist, biologist, and poet.
Once Mexico's top law-enforcement official as secretary of public security, this man was convicted in a Brooklyn courtroom in 2023 for taking millions in bribes from the Sinaloa Cartel — who is he?
Genaro García Luna: Mexican politician and convicted felon (born 1968)
With the symbol Au and atomic number 79, this soft, dense element is so unreactive that only platinum sits below it — and it often turns up as native nuggets in riverbeds. What is it?
Gold: Chemical element with atomic number 79 (Au). Chemically, gold is a transition metal, a group 11 element, and one of the noble metals.
Combined with obstetrics as a joint medical specialty and touching on everything from family planning to pelvic reconstructive surgery, which field focuses on the female reproductive system?
Gynaecology: Medical area for women's reproductive health.

Often triggered by a preceding throat infection, this childhood autoimmune disease causes raised skin bruising, joint pain, and sometimes kidney trouble from IgA immune-complex deposits — what is it called?
Henoch–Schönlein purpura: Autoimmune vascular inflammatory disease.
Defined today as exactly 3,600 seconds, this unit of time was originally a variable measure equal to one-twelfth of the night or day in the ancient Near East — which unit?
Hour: Unit of time equal to 60 minutes.
This physical phenomenon describes how a system's current state depends on its past history, forming looping curves in magnets and giving hard disk drives their memory — what is it?
Hysteresis: Dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.
This condition restricts blood flow to tissue, starving cells of oxygen and nutrients due to causes like thrombosis or embolism — what's it called?
Ischemia: Restriction in blood supply to tissues.
This British chemical engineer founded a major chemicals group in 1998 and later became a minority shareholder with control over football operations at Manchester United — who is he?
Jim Ratcliffe: British engineer and businessman (born 1952)
Its subfamily name literally means 'large foot,' it's native to Australia and New Guinea, and a 2019 government tally counted some 42.8 million of them in harvest areas. Which marsupial?
Kangaroo: Marsupial of the family Macropodidae.
About 1.5 metres long and beginning at the cecum via the ileocecal valve, this final section of the human gut absorbs water and salt before waste reaches the rectum — what part of the body is it?
Large intestine: Last part of the digestive system in vertebrates.
Sometimes called the paleomammalian cortex, this set of brain structures — including the amygdala — governs emotion, motivation, and long-term memory — what is it called?
Limbic system: Set of brain structures involved in emotion and motivation. Its various components support a variety of functions including emotion, behavior, long-term memory, and olfaction.

This German fluid dynamicist built the mathematical foundations of subsonic aerodynamics, identifying the 'boundary layer' and lifting-line theory — and lent his name to a dimensionless number. Who was he?

First isolated in the 1770s and carrying atomic number 25, this hard, silvery transition metal is a key alloying agent in stainless steel and also an essential trace nutrient in the human diet — which element?
Manganese: Chemical element with atomic number 25 (Mn)

First synthesized near Darmstadt in 1982, this fleeting synthetic element — its most stable isotope lasts mere seconds — was named for the Austrian-Swedish nuclear physicist Lise Meitner. Which element is it?
Meitnerium: Chemical element with atomic number 109 (Mt)
North of the Arctic Circle in summer, this phenomenon keeps the sky lit long after the clock strikes twelve — what is it called?
Midnight sun: Natural phenomenon when daylight lasts for a whole day.

Nicknamed the Swiss cheese plant for its perforated leaves, this houseplant native to southern Mexico and Central America produces a fruit that's edible once ripe, despite needle-like calcium oxalate crystals elsewhere in the plant — what is its scientific name?
Monstera deliciosa: Species of plant. Monstera deliciosa, the Swiss cheese plant or split-leaf philodendron, is a species of flowering plant.
Made of the same tough protein as claws, hooves, and horns, this protective plate covers the tip of your fingers and toes — what is it?
Nail (anatomy): Hard keratin protection of digit.
Sold under the brand name Macrobid, this antibacterial drug treats lower urinary tract infections but isn't effective against kidney infections. What is it?
Nitrofurantoin: Antibacterial drug. Nitrofurantoin, sold under the brand name Macrobid among others, is an antibacterial medication of the nitrofuran class.
Sold under the brand name Prilosec, this proton-pump inhibitor treats acid reflux and peptic ulcers — what is it?
Omeprazole: Medication to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease and other conditions.
Located behind the stomach, this gland is 99 percent exocrine yet still secretes insulin and glucagon to regulate blood sugar — which organ?
Pancreas: Organ of the digestive system and endocrine system of vertebrates.
A famous singer known for her CCTV New Year's Gala appearances, she has served as China's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?
Peng Liyuan: First Lady of China since 2012. Peng also sang the theme songs of several popular TV series, such as The Water Margin (1998).

So reactive that it never appears uncombined in nature, this element was famously isolated in 1669 by Hennig Brand — the scientific community's first documented discovery of an element — and comes in white and red forms. Which one is it?
Phosphorus: Chemical element with atomic number 15 (P)
With a half-life of just 138 days, this rare radioactive element occurs only in trace amounts within uranium ore and is chemically similar to selenium — what is it?
Polonium: Chemical element with atomic number 84 (Po)
Genetic studies trace this most widely cultivated apricot species to Central Asia, though its scientific name nods to a country in the Caucasus — what is it?
Prunus armeniaca: Species of apricot. The native range is somewhat uncertain due to its extensive prehistoric cultivation.
About the size of a house cat, this nocturnal herbivorous marsupial thrives on Rottnest Island near Perth and is the only member of its genus — what is it?
Quokka: Small marsupial from southwestern Australia.

Covering more than 200 conditions from arthritis to soft-tissue pain syndromes, this umbrella term for chronic joint and connective-tissue pain gives its name to a whole medical specialty — what is it called?
Rheumatism: Medical conditions affecting the joints or connective tissue.
Known as rue or 'herb-of-grace,' this Mediterranean plant is prized for its bluish leaves and doubles as an insect repellent — which species?
Ruta graveolens: Species of plant. Ruta graveolens, commonly known as rue, common rue, ruda, arruda or herb-of-grace, is a species of the genus Ruta grown as an ornamental plant and herb.
This group of autoimmune diseases causes thickened skin and poor blood flow to the fingers and toes, with one form known as CREST syndrome — what is it called?
Scleroderma: Group of autoimmune diseases resulting in abnormal growth of connective tissue.
This Japanese army medical officer led a biological and chemical warfare unit in Japanese-occupied Manchuria during World War II and was later granted immunity — who is he?
Shirō Ishii: Japanese biological weapons specialist (1892–1959)
Raised in the Bronx by Puerto Rican-born parents after her father's early death, this Princeton and Yale Law graduate became the third woman ever named to the U.S. Supreme Court — who is she?
Sonia Sotomayor: US Supreme Court justice since 2009.

Often triggered by medications like lamotrigine or allopurinol, this severe skin reaction starts with flu-like symptoms before the skin begins to blister, peel, and affect mucous membranes — what is this condition called?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome: Skin disease. The most common cause is certain medications such as lamotrigine, carbamazepine, allopurinol, sulfonamide antibiotics and nevirapine.

This red-orange, sublimable heterocyclic solid is a stable aminoxyl radical used as a spin probe in electron spin resonance spectroscopy and as a mediator in controlled radical polymerization — what's this compound commonly called?
Discovered via its telltale green spectral line in 1861, this silvery post-transition metal takes its name from the Greek word for a green shoot — which element?
Thallium: Chemical element with atomic number 81 (Tl)
Called the "Father of Japanese Botany," this grammar-school dropout collected over 500,000 plant specimens and earned a doctorate — and his birthday is now Botany Day in Japan. Who was he?
Also known as 45,X, which chromosomal condition affects only females who are born with a single X chromosome instead of two, often causing short stature and a webbed neck?
Turner syndrome: X chromosome monosomy. Small chin (micrognathia), loose folds of skin on the neck, slanted eyelids and prominent ears are found in Turner syndrome, though not all will show it.
Defined by a vertebral column shielding the spinal cord and a cranium guarding the brain, this group of some 65,000 species is the largest ranked grouping in the phylum Chordata — what is it?

With black-tipped wings and long red legs and bill, this long-distance migrant famously avoids the open Mediterranean, detouring instead via Gibraltar or the Levant on its way to African wintering grounds — which bird is it?
White stork: Species of bird. The white stork (Ciconia ciconia) is a large bird in the stork family, Ciconiidae.
This spider's ghoulish nickname, the 'Nosferatu spider,' references a classic vampire — which species is it?
Zoropsis spinimana: Species of spider. Zoropsis spinimana, also known as Nosferatu spider, is a spider species belonging to the family Zoropsidae.
What is the chemical symbol for boron?
The symbol for boron is B. Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.

In what year was Cher born?
Cher (SHAIR; legally mononymous; born Cheryl Sarkisian, May 20, 1946) is an American singer and actress.
In what year was Olga Kurylenko born?
Olga Kurylenko: Olga Kostyantynivna Kurylenko (born 14 November 1979) is a Ukrainian-born French actress and former model.
In what year was Gal Gadot born?
Gal Gadot (Hebrew: גל גדות, pronounced [ˈɡal ɡaˈdot]; born 30 April 1985) is an Israeli actress.
In what year was Lily-Rose Depp born?
Lily-Rose Depp: Lily-Rose Melody Depp (born May 27, 1999) is a French and American actress and singer.
In what year was Fran Drescher born?
Fran Drescher: Francine Joy Drescher (born September 30, 1957) is an American actress, writer, comedian, producer, and former trade union leader.
In what year was Chuck Norris born?
Chuck Norris: Carlos Ray "Chuck" Norris (March 10, 1940 – March 19, 2026) was an American martial artist, actor, screenwriter, and author.
In what year was Prabhas born?
Prabhas made his acting debut with the drama Eeswar (2002) and later attained his breakthrough with the action romance Varsham (2004).
In what year was George Lucas born?
George Lucas: George Walton Lucas Jr. (born May 14, 1944) is an American filmmaker and philanthropist.
In what year was Golshifteh Farahani born?
